feed.title: BIP Proposal: Stateless PSBT Coordination (Blind Relay)

entry.title: BIP Proposal: Stateless PSBT Coordination (Blind Relay)
entry.summary:
Version 4.2.0 of the Signing Room coordinator, along with version 2.2.0 of the signing-room/sdk, introduces comprehensive end-to-end support for 2-round MuSig2 Taproot keypath ceremonies, aligning with BIP-327 and BIP-373 standards. This implementation leverages an ephemeral, operator-blind relay to maintain privacy and security throughout the signing process.
The BIP draft has been updated to clearly define a two-part ceremony state machine. The first round focuses on the initial setup and public nonce collection, while the second round is dedicated to aggregating partial signatures. This structure ensures that the relay remains completely blind to ceremony details, thereby enhancing participant confidentiality and protocol robustness.
Significant optimization has also been applied to the audit log wire protocol. Instead of broadcasting full arrays of audit logs repeatedly, the system now dispatches only incremental updates supplemented by a continuously updated SHA-256 hash chain, referred to as chainHash. This approach not only reduces network bandwidth consumption but also provides tamper-evidence that clients can independently verify, thus improving both efficiency and trustworthiness.
Further technical details and the complete set of release notes are available at [this release page](https://github.com/scarlin90/signingroom/releases/tag/v4.2.0). For direct access to the revised BIP draft, refer to [the latest document here](https://github.com/scarlin90/bip-stateless-psbt-coordination/blob/d1e3fc8f5b4d02551a1528d23c094f6df56cd259/bip-draft.md).
